sentences.text:
These appeals are filed by the appellants-petitioners challenging the common judgment and award dated 17.10.2012 passed in MVC.Nos.115/2010 and 113/2010 by the MACT-No.VII, Bijapur (for Bhagirathi W/O Suresh Chougale vs Parvati W/O Mruttunjay Vastrad And Anr on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131554756/
2 short 'the Tribunal').
2.
Though this matter is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal 4.
Learned counsel for the appellants-petitioners in both cases submits that the tribunal has not passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts so also awarded meager compensation.

He further submits that the tribunal has erred in holding that the offending vehicle was not insured with the insurance as on the date of the accident, however the Insurance Company has satisfied the award amount in MVC No.1425, 1426 and 1427 of 2012 on the file of the Member MACT-XII, Bijapur, arising out of the same accident.
He further submits that he has filed a memo along with copy of the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, he sought for remand the matter to the tribunal for disposal in accordance with law.
5. The memo is taken on record.
I have perused memo along with copy of policy bearing No.151300/31/07/01/00009657 valid from 20.02.2008 to 19.02.2009.
This policy pertains to the vehicle bearing No.KA- 28/4508 Taxi maxicab.
Hence, it is clear that the policy was in force as on the date of the accident.
6. The tribunal has also not considered the notional income as per the Lok Adalath chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.

Hence, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also in view of the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it is just and proper to remand the matter to the tribunal for fresh consideration.

7. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) Both the appeals are allowed and remanded.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal is set aside.

(c) The matter is remitted back to the tribunal for deciding the matter afresh by permitting both the parties to adduce their oral and documentary evidence, if any, and dispose of the case in accordance with law.
(d) The parties shall appear before the Court of the tribunal, on 30.05.2023 without awaiting any further notice.
Thereafter, the tribunal shall dispose of the case within an outer limit of three months from the date of appearance of the parties.
(e) Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of the judgment forthwith.
